done_when: A job permission card stays bounded across many runs, the reconciler skips cards with nothing pending without loading their payload, a migration shrinks existing oversized cards, and the runtime warns when its main thread is blocked, proven by tests including one that grows a card past 1,000 runs

findings.body: Denied one-time requests still grow the card indefinitely. Production gives each once-request a distinct identity (`job-permission-durability-wiring.ts:236–239`), and reconciliation finishes a denial in state `denied` (`job-permission-reconciler.ts:552`). This settlement predicate excludes that state, so every denied request remains pending. `livingCardNeeds` retains all denials (`job-permission-card-projection.ts:327`), and each new revision stores every retained need in `representedNeeds` (lines 232–235), despite limiting visible rows. Heartbeats consequently keep loading and rewriting the accumulated needs and growing revision payloads. The migration excludes denials too (lines 121–127). Bound older terminal once-denials on writes and in the migration, preserving the required current receipt and replay behavior, and cover repeated denials in the Postgres regression test.
